executive_summary: Markets enter Wednesday caught between a powerful semiconductor rebound — SOXX +5.45%, Intel +8.64%, AMD +8.11% on Monday — and a grinding US-Iran military conflict now in its 10th consecutive day of strikes with Brent crude above $91. Tonight's after-bell earnings from Alphabet (EPS +23% expected) and Tesla ($0.47 EPS consensus) will set the tone for the rest of mega-cap earnings week, with AMD's Advancing AI conference and Intel's Q2 report on Thursday adding semiconductor fuel. The Fed remains pinned at 3.50-3.75% with new Chair Warsh signaling hawkish intent as June CPI headline sits at 3.5% and oil threatens re-acceleration. The S&P 500 closed at 7,509 (+0.89%) Tuesday, snapping a three-day slide, but futures are mixed overnight with Dow futures down ~0.2% as the geopolitical overhang persists.

macro_events.title: US-Iran Military Conflict — 10+ Days of Strikes, 3 US Service Members Killed
macro_events.causal_chain: US completes 10th consecutive night of strikes on Iran → Iran retaliates, tanker struck near Strait of Hormuz → 21% of global oil trade and 20% of LNG transits through Hormuz → war-risk insurance premiums spike on VLCCs → Brent breaks $91 (+2.26%), WTI $84+ → Houthi rebels threaten Saudi maritime traffic in Red Sea → Saudi crude tanker forced to reverse course → Asian refiners reroute via Cape of Good Hope (+12-14 days, +$2M/trip) → Qatar LNG-to-Europe at risk → headline inflation expectations rise → Fed forced to hold rates at 3.50-3.75% longer → USD strengthens on safe-haven flows → EM oil importers (India, Turkey, Indonesia) currencies weaken
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East → Global energy markets → US/Europe/Asia consumers → EM FX
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent surged +15% in 24 hours, tanker stocks rallied 20-35% in one week. Current conflict is more sustained than Abqaiq, suggesting prolonged premium.
macro_events.counterargument: Iran signaled willingness to pursue diplomacy over the weekend; US may seek negotiated de-escalation. A rapid ceasefire could drop Brent $10+ and unwind the war premium.

macro_events.title: Fed Policy Paralysis — Warsh Hawkish, Rates Stuck at 3.50-3.75%
macro_events.causal_chain: New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh (took office May 22, 2026) urges no repeat of past delays in raising rates → signals hawkish lean despite slowing core inflation → fed funds at 3.50-3.75%, FOMC July 28-29 expected hold → June CPI headline 3.5% YoY but core 2.6% → oil above $90 threatens re-acceleration of headline → real rates deeply restrictive at ~4.6% 10Y → 20Y bond auction today tests long-end demand → elevated cost of capital squeezes housing, small-cap, EM borrowers → all 32 large banks passed 2026 stress test (stability signal) → but restrictive policy weighing on credit growth
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US monetary policy → Global interest rates → EM funding costs
macro_events.historical_analog: Late 2018 Fed tightening cycle — Powell paused after market volatility forced a rethink. Warsh may face similar pressure if oil-driven inflation conflicts with slowing growth.
macro_events.counterargument: Core inflation at 2.6% is approaching target; energy-driven headline could fade quickly if Iran diplomacy succeeds. The Fed may pivot dovish faster than markets expect.
